#table(stroke: none, columns: 6, align: (center, center, center, center, center, center, ), table.vline(stroke: .5pt, x: 0), table.vline(stroke: .5pt, x: 1), table.vline(stroke: .5pt, x: 2), table.vline(stroke: .5pt, x: 3), table.vline(stroke: .5pt, x: 4), table.vline(stroke: .5pt, x: 5), table.vline(stroke: .5pt, x: 6), table.hline(stroke: .5pt), [$x$], [2], [3], [5], [8], [13], table.hline(stroke: .5pt), [$f(x)$], [1], [4], [-2], [3], [6], table.hline(stroke: .5pt));

Let $f$ be a function that is twice differentiable for all real numbers. The table above gives values of $f$ for selected points in the closed interval $2 <= x <= 13$.

(a) Estimate $f'(4)$. Show the work that leads to your answer.

(b) Evaluate $integral_(2)^(13)lr((3 - 5 f'(x))) d x$. Show the work that leads to your answer.

(c) Use a left Riemann sum with subintervals indicated by the data in the table to approximate $integral_(2)^(13) f(x) d x$. Show the work that leads to your answer.

(d) Suppose $f'(5)= 3$ and $f''(x)< 0$ for all $x$ in the closed interval $5 <= x <= 8$. Use the line tangent to the graph of $f$ at $x = 5$ to show that $f(7) <= 4$. Use the secant line for the graph of $f$ on $5 <= x <= 8$ to show that $f(7) >= frac(4,3)$.
